text:
Alex H: Heads-up — nightly int8 suite showed a 6% p50 regression on AWQ weight-only after we flipped default group_size=32 last night. noticed mostly on long-context chat workloads.
Maya L: ugh. saw the alert too. do we know if it's kernel dispatch or packing overhead?
Alex H: quick diffs from profiler: more time in `pack_serial` and `pack-memcopy` vs before. kernel selection moved from `awq_int8_group16_fwd` -> `awq_int8_group32_fwd` for ~40% of requests.
perf-bot: nightly-run/awq-int8: p50 72ms -> 76.5ms (+6.25%), tokens/s 1420 -> 1310 (-7.7%). kv-cache hit rate 0.88 -> 0.83.
Kevin P: could be two things: larger group size reduces kernel overhead per weight but increases packing alignment cost and memory ops; also group32 may not vectorize well on certain kernels/SMs.
Priya S: do we have end-to-end traces that correlate pack time vs kv hotpath? if pack spikes, batching heuristics can shrink batch size -> worse throughput.
Alex H: attached small trace snippet from perf tool:
```
# sample trace (aggregated)
pack_serial: total=0.92ms (prev=0.44ms)
pack-memcopy: total=0.37ms (prev=0.18ms)
kernel_awq_group32_fwd: total=0.58ms (prev=0.62ms)
kv_lookup: 0.12ms (prev=0.09ms), miss-rate +4.5%
```
Maya L: interesting that kernel time slightly improved but overall p50 worse -> points to pack + kv interactions. maybe packing now delays KV cache priming causing misses.
Kevin P: hypothesis: pack is now larger per-op so it blocks the CPU thread and pushes KV prefetch later. If prefetch window is narrow, KV misses increase.
Priya S: i'll run microbench: `./tools/bench --model=redwood/7b-awq --quant=awq-int8 --group=32 --batch=1 --profile=kv,pack,kernel` and same for group=16/8. will post numbers.
Alex H: please also capture `nvprof` flame + `perf` on host to check memcpy stalls.
perf-bot: triage label added: perf/regression, owner: @Priya S
Maya L: if this is packing ordering, interim mitigation could be: - revert default to group=16, or - enable overlapping pack+kv-prefetch (we have proto for pack prefetch in runtime).
Kevin P: the proto overlap helped in my local sims — reduced pack blocking by ~30% but requires careful KV prefetch scheduling.
Priya S: quick numbers from first microbench (group=32 vs group=16):
- group=32: tokens/s 1285, p50=78ms, pack_time=0.91ms
- group=16: tokens/s 1398, p50=71ms, pack_time=0.46ms
So pack_time roughly doubled and throughput dropped accordingly.
Alex H: that's pretty conclusive. can we try enabling `runtime.config.overlap_pack_prefetch=true` in dev env to see if kv miss rate recovers?
Priya S: doing that now on canary cluster. also will run GPTQ quantized variant to compare (awq vs gptq differences).
Maya L: curious about calibration impact — AWQ calibration shrinks per-group metadata, but group32 may have larger alignment padding and cause more memcpy. GPTQ might behave differently.
Kevin P: note for release notes: changing default group size can have non-obvious perf regressions due to runtime packing interplay. documentable lesson.
Priya S: canary results: overlap_pack_prefetch=true => kv hit-rate 0.86 (was 0.83), p50 down to 73.2ms. improvement but still worse than group16 baseline.
Alex H: action items: 1) revert default to group=16 for now in canary and prod config; 2) prioritize overlap pack prefetch work + add microbench gating; 3) add kernel selection telemetry to record pack_time/kerneltime ratio per request.
Maya L: agree. i'll open a quick RFC for pack-prefetch rollout + perf dashboards.
Priya S: creating issue + linking bench results. tagging @Kevin P for kernel follow-up.
Kevin P: will look into optimizing memcopy path and check if group32 can be packed with smaller intermediate buffer to reduce wall time.
Alex H: thanks all. small note: if anyone runs more benches, please include `--kv-warmup=1` flag to see cold vs warmed behavior.
Maya L: :thumbsup:
Priya S: filing thread summary in the perf board.
Alex H: closing loop tomorrow after we validate canary.
